back: Communicating with customers to inform them about a product and persuade them to buy it.
Inform, persuade, remind, build brand image, increase sales and market share.
Informative gives facts (price, features, where to buy); persuasive creates a desire to buy.
Radio, television, newspapers and magazines, billboards, leaflets, social media, targeted digital messages, vehicles and sponsorship.
Price offers, coupons and vouchers, free samples, competitions, loyalty schemes, gifts, point-of-sale displays.
Consider budget, target market and the media they use, product, life-cycle stage, competitors and size of market.
Attention, Interest, Desire, Action: a checklist for designing an advertisement.
Effects are usually short-term; frequent offers cut profit and can make the brand look cheap.
Advertising by a whole industry for a type of product (e.g. "eat more beef") rather than one brand.
